item.title: Turning Zeeman splitting into switchable charge polarization in a double quantum dot
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — A uniform Zeeman field Mz modulates and can completely reverse single-electron charge polarization PL−PR in an asymmetric double quantum dot without altering electrostatic detuning.

Grade 0.510 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · Chi Sun, Jacob Linder

Figure

Plots maximum change in dot occupation probabilities ΔPL,Rmax⁡ across bare gate levels (v1,v2) under a swept Zeeman field |Mz|≤1, showing substantial charge transfer while maintaining PN=1≃1.

Asks

Can a spatially uniform magnetic Zeeman field control left-right charge polarization in an open double quantum dot?

But

Interaction-dominated regime where interdot tunneling t12 and lead coupling γ are smaller than Coulomb interactions Ui,U12; wide-band limit for electronic reservoirs.

Tools

Green's-function equation-of-motion (EOM) · Hubbard-Anderson-type DQD Hamiltonian · 16-state density-correlation hierarchy

Abstract

A magnetic field that acts identically on two quantum dots is not expected to move charge between them. Nevertheless, we show that a uniform Zeeman field can strongly reconfigure and even reverse the single-electron charge polarization of an asymmetric open double quantum dot. Using a symmetry-preserving Green's-function equation-of-motion approach, we identify regimes where the preferred dot occupation reverses while the system remains in the single-electron charge sector. Two distinct mechanisms produce this behavior. Unequal gate levels produce different occupation responses because the Zeeman-shifted resonances lie at different positions relative to the reservoir chemical potential, whereas unequal onsite interactions distinguish the dots through their many-body addition spectra. Coulomb blockade stabilizes the single-electron sector, causing the reservoir-mediated response to appear as spatial charge redistribution rather than a change in total occupation. Our results establish a mechanism for magnetic control of charge polarization at fixed electrostatic detuning.

item.title: Super-resolution Control of Two-dimensional Quantum Emitters
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — AFM-based local Stark gating resolves and localizes individual interlayer excitonic quantum emitters separated by dD3−D4=(39±19) nm and dD1−D2=(41±15) nm, with single-emitter localization resolution limit ΔyD1≃20 nm.

Grade 0.487 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · Bosai Lyu, Valeria Vento, Ludivine Fausten, Daniel Suarez-Forero, Klevis Domi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Alberto Morpurgo, Iaroslav Gaponenko, Patrycja Paruch, Ajit Srivastava

Figure

PL emission and Stark shifts under AFM tip raster scanning. Extracted sub-diffraction spatial map of 7 individual localized emitters in a 250 nm×250 nm area with emitter separations down to roughly 40 nm.

Asks

Can subwavelength-confined 2D quantum emitters be spatially resolved and individually controlled in energy, charge state, and radiative lifetime beyond the optical diffraction limit?

But

Base temperature 4 K in cryostat; top and bottom hBN flake thicknesses between 15 nm and 20 nm; emitter position extraction relies on uniform in-plane dipole offset across single domain.

Tools

Quantum Optical Super-resolution Microscope (QOSMic) · Conducting AFM cantilever local gate · Cryogenic confocal PL spectroscopy · hBN-encapsulated MoSe₂/WSe₂ heterobilayers · Time-resolved single-photon counting

Abstract

Localized interlayer excitons in semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide heterobilayers are quantum emitters with a static electric dipole moment, making them excellent nanoscale charge sensors to probe correlated quantum phases in a proximal layer. These emitters are electrically tunable and inherit spin-valley selection rules, yet their deterministic spatial control remains challenging due to subwavelength confinement. Here, we present a platform that combines cryogenic optical spectroscopy with scanning probe microscopy to investigate trapped interlayer excitons in WSe₂/MoSe₂ bilayers. By exploiting AFM-based local Stark shift, we achieve super-resolution localization of emitters separated by only a few tens of nanometers and demonstrate deterministic control of individual charge states, including trion formation, opening a path towards coherent inter-dot coupling. Time-resolved measurements reveal tip-induced modification of the electromagnetic vacuum around individual emitters, thus controlling their radiative emission. Our multi-point charge sensing platform with optical readout is particularly well-suited to study fractionalization and anyon dynamics in semiconducting FCIs.

item.title: Multi-dimensional spectroscopy of mobile excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Microscopic theory with continuous exciton momenta reproduces multidimensional coherent spectroscopy peak hierarchies, broadening, and cross-peak interference in monolayer MoSe2 via phase-space filling polaron interactions.

Grade 0.457 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Driven coherent oscillations of a single electron spin in a quantum dot” · Ned Wheaton, Jeffrey A. Davis, Jesper Levinsen, Meera M. Parish

Figure

Interaction energy shifts per area as a function of Fermi energy EF/εT for attractive-attractive, attractive-repulsive, and repulsive-repulsive polaron pairs, showing transition from attractive to repulsive polaron-polaron interactions at higher doping.

Asks

How do continuous momentum degrees of freedom and microscopic many-body interactions shape multidimensional coherent spectroscopy spectra of excitons and exciton-polarons in 2D semiconductors?

Before

Calculated attractive-polaron-attractive-polaron interaction strengths differ by less than 16% at EF/εT=1 and under 10% for EF/εT≲0.4 compared to the Chevy ansatz in Ref. [31] (Sidler et al., 2017).

But

Dipole approximation for light-matter coupling; pure ground state; identical co-circular excitons; electron-electron and exciton-exciton exchange processes neglected.

Tools

Time-dependent perturbation theory · Chevy ansatz / truncation of the basis · Bethe-Salpeter-like equations of motion · Born approximation

Abstract

Multi-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (MDCS) goes beyond standard linear-response probes and provides a powerful tool for investigating correlations between quasiparticles such as excitons (bound electron-hole pairs). Here we present a microscopic theory of MDCS that accounts for the delocalized nature of excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors. In contrast to the more phenomenological few-level approaches typically employed for modelling MDCS, our theory features mobile excitons with continuous momentum degrees of freedom. We find that the energy continuum associated with exciton momenta is crucial for producing interaction-induced decoherence, as well as capturing the interference between different exciton-polaron quasiparticles in the case of charge-doped semiconductors. Crucially, our calculated MDCS spectra agree well with recent experiments on doped monolayer MoSe₂ [Hao et al., Nature Communications 8, 15552 (2017)], and they suggest that the interactions between exciton polarons depend strongly on phase-space filling effects, where exciton polarons compete for electrons. Our results demonstrate that microscopic approaches allow one to gain new insights from the fine structure of MDCS on two-dimensional semiconductors, and they illustrate the utility of microscopic approaches to modelling MDCS experiments more generally.

item.title: Crystal-phase quantum dots in AlGaAs nanowires
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Crystal-phase quantum dots in AlGaAs nanowire cores achieve narrow exciton and biexciton linewidths of 104 µeV and 61 µeV (±4 µeV) with 1 ns exciton lifetime indicating type-I band alignment.

Grade 0.437 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Driven coherent oscillations of a single electron spin in a quantum dot” · Rohan Radhakrishnan, Rodion Reznik, Gilles Patriarche, Lorenzo Leandro, Igor Ilkiv, Anna Andreeva, Artem Khrebtov, George Cirlin, Nika Akopian

Figure

Excitation power dependence, decay kinetics, and photon correlation histograms showing clean exciton-biexciton emission, 1 ns radiative lifetime, and antibunching from an AlGaAs crystal-phase quantum dot.

Asks

Can crystal-phase quantum dots in AlGaAs nanowires overcome the broad emission linewidths and type-II band alignment typical of binary crystal-phase quantum dots?

Before

Crystal-phase quantum dots in binary semiconductors such as InP and GaAs typically exhibit emission linewidths in the meV range and exciton lifetimes of tens of nanoseconds.

But

Nanowire core diameter 7 to 20 nm; zincblende insertion density 15 to 50 insertions/µm; timing resolution of correlation measurements limited by detector jitter (FWHM ≳505 ps or 110 ps).

Tools

molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) · HAADF-STEM · energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) · micro-photoluminescence · Hanbury Brown and Twiss interferometry

Abstract

Crystal-phase quantum dots (CPQDs)unicodex2014quantum dots in nanowires defined by crystal structure rather than material compositionunicodex2014constitute the only platform capable of fabricating quantum-dot arrays with the ultimate precision of a single atomic layer. This intrinsic control yields perfectly aligned quantum dots with atomically sharp interfaces, providing a unique pathway toward scalable quantum-dot-based photonic quantum technologies. To date, CPQDs have been studied primarily in binary semiconductors, such as InP and GaAs, where their emission linewidths are typically in the meV range, thereby limiting their technological potential. Here, we report, for the first time, CPQDs in AlGaAs nanowires and show bright single-photon emission with linewidths as narrow as 61 μeV and low background emission, demonstrating optical quality well beyond typical CPQDs. We attribute this performance to a type-I band alignment, as suggested by an exciton lifetime of 1 ns, significantly shorter than that typically observed in type-II CPQDs. Additionally, we observe an exciton fine-structure splitting and a Zeeman splitting, as commonly observed in standard type-I self-assembled quantum dots.
